titleEn: Breathe Out—A White Cloud of Breath!

pages.text: "Give back my scarf!" Yuki stamped on the porch. Brown dog Momo held the vermilion scarf's end and ran into the yard, looking back with a waving tail.
"I'm going outside! Give it back!" Yuki shouted, voice ringing across the yard. Momo laid their ears down and slipped beneath the porch.
The space was dark and narrow. Yuki could not see the scarf. "Come out now!" A palm banged on a board. Momo went farther in.
Grandma came onto the porch in gray layered clothes. "You feel hot inside, don't you? Come stand at the edge." Yuki went over, breathing angrily.
"Breathe slowly in through your nose, then out through your mouth." Yuki did it. A fluffy white cloud came out!
"What's that?" "Your hot breath." The white cloud drifted into the yard and disappeared. Yuki breathed out again. Another white cloud went out and faded.
Each breath made Yuki feel cooler inside. "Breathe Out—A White Cloud of Breath!" Their angry shoulders slowly settled.
"I won't shout now," Yuki told Momo quietly. A nose and front paws emerged. The scarf lay on a board. Yuki wrapped it around their neck and fixed the knot.
But Momo grabbed the end again! Anger rose. Yuki went to the porch's edge and breathed out. A white cloud appeared and faded. "One, stop a moment! Two, breathe out! Three, then talk!"

As Yuki turned toward the yard, Grandma warmed their cold hands between hers. "Let anger out in your breath, instead of your voice." Yuki's toes already pointed outside. "Breathe Out—A White Cloud of Breath!"
